For a reversible walk on a weighted tree,

\[
C_{ij}=2\Big(\sum_{e}c_e\Big)R_{\rm eff}(i,j),
\]

and on a tree the effective resistance is the sum of edge resistances along the unique path.

The given commute times behave like additive tree distances:

\[
C_{13}=10=4+6=C_{12}+C_{23},
\]
so vertex \(2\) lies between \(1\) and \(3\). Also,

\[
C_{24}=18=6+12=C_{23}+C_{34},
\]
so vertex \(3\) lies between \(2\) and \(4\). Hence the tree is the path

\[
1-2-3-4,
\]

with commute-length edges \(4,6,12\). Therefore

\[
C_{14}=4+6+12=22.
\]

Let the conductances on \(12,23,34\) be \(a,b,c\). Since edge commute lengths are proportional to \(1/a,1/b,1/c\),

\[
a:b:c=\frac14:\frac16:\frac1{12}=3:2:1.
\]

Thus

\[
P(2,1)=\frac35,\quad P(2,3)=\frac25,
\]
\[
P(3,2)=\frac23,\quad P(3,4)=\frac13.
\]

Let \(h_i=\mathbb E_iT_4\). Then

\[
h_4=0,\quad h_1=1+h_2,
\]
\[
h_2=1+\frac35h_1+\frac25h_3,
\]
\[
h_3=1+\frac23h_2.
\]

Solving gives

\[
h_2=15,\quad h_1=16,\quad h_3=11.
\]

So

\[
\mathbb E_1T_4=16.
\]

For second moments \(s_i=\mathbb E_i(T_4^2)\),

\[
s_i=1+2\sum_jP(i,j)h_j+\sum_jP(i,j)s_j.
\]

Using \(h_1=16,h_2=15,h_3=11\),

\[
s_1=1+2h_2+s_2=31+s_2,
\]
\[
s_3=1+\frac43h_2+\frac23s_2=21+\frac23s_2,
\]
\[
s_2=1+2\left(\frac35h_1+\frac25h_3\right)+\frac35s_1+\frac25s_3.
\]

This gives \(s_2=420\), hence \(s_1=451\). Therefore

\[
\operatorname{Var}_1(T_4)=s_1-h_1^2=451-16^2=195.
\]

\[
\boxed{(C_{14},\mathbb E_1T_4,\operatorname{Var}_1(T_4))=(22,16,195)}
\]
